newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Toyota confirms plan to expand Australian output.
newsitem.headline: Toyota confirms plan to expand Australian output.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said in Monday it planned to expand its Australian manufacturing operations to produce a new large car for the domestic market.

The new 3000cc six-cylinder model, based on the Avalon made for the U.S. market, would help take production at the company's Altona plant in Melbourne to 100,00 units from 80,000 a year, company officials said. "The new car is part of a development programme for Toyota Australia which will need substantial capital investment on top of the A$1.8 billion put in over the past decade," Toyota said in a statement released in Melbourne.
"In terms of its genesis, the new car will be based on the Avalon, currently manufactured in the United States and substantially modified and adapted for Australia," Toyota said.

The company, confirming a report in the Nihon Keizai Shimbun newspaper on Sunday, said the new capacity would not involve a new production line but would require investment in new equipment such as production robots. The first of the new vehicles is scheduled to roll off the production line in 2000.

"The Australian government recently announced policy settings for the local car industry which in Toyota's view are positive and constructive," Toyota Motor Corp president Hiroshi Okuda said in a statement prepared for delivery in Melbourne.
"I'm pleased to say that this policy direction gives us the confidence to proceed with plans for Australia," he said.
The move comes after Australia decided not to cut tariffs on car imports by as much as originally planned.

"As a priority, we need to lift our production capacity to meet an expected increase in demand in both our domestic and export markets," Toyota Australia president Sam Komori said in a statement prepared for delivery at a news conference.
